parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Jashubhai, father-in-law, mother-in-law, brother-in-law, uncle-in-law and wife of brother-in-law

facts_of_case: Marriage took place in 1997. Two children were born. Husband suffered serious ailments. Complainant left for UK in 2009. Customary divorce was signed in 2010. Son died on 24.01.2010.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to set aside a document to prove that it was obtained by fraud, coercion, or undue influence.
legal_principles.held: Considering the nature of dispute between the widow-respondent No.2 and her in-laws and deed of customary divorce, prima facie it appears that the respondent No.2-complainant-widow had raised specific objection

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot claim relief by creating a document that is not acceptable to them and then seek to set it aside.
legal_principles.held: The complainant also signed the customary divorce deed on 29.01.2010 with specific note that she had signed under compulsion and duress of her in-laws

outcome.final_order: Petitioner's prayer to quash and set aside criminal complaint is allowed.
